The relevant positive threshold for stronger dependency in this direction is about +0.025. The upper bound is below that threshold, and the interval includes no meaningful evidence of stronger RPL11 dependency in the claimed direction. This rejects the MYC-program/RPL11 association in the supplied dataset; I keep the investigation closed.

For H161 (CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A-intact within TP53-loss lines on MDM2 dependency), discovery R95 was +0.111 with interval +0.035 to +0.186, cells 81 versus 325, above the approximate MDM2 threshold of +0.027. New independent validation R106 was +0.115 with stringent interval +0.002 to +0.227, cells 95 versus 310. Validation confirms direction and excludes zero under the stringent validation criterion, but its lower bound is near zero and below the 10-percent clinical threshold. Thus the TP53-loss-specific magnitude is less certain than the global CDKN2A/MDM2 association. I accept H161 as a dataset-specific association based on discovery plus consistent validation, but keep the investigation active because independent evidence alone does not establish a clinically meaningful effect size within TP53-loss cells. This is not a causal or generalizable claim.

Supported findings. The supplied lung cell-line dataset now supports five robust marker-dependency axes, all as associations rather than causal dependencies: MSI-high is associated with far stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4 loss is associated with far stronger SMARCA2 dependency, including in ARID1A-intact, ARID1A-loss, adenocarcinoma, CDKN2A-intact, and other marker-intact contexts; KEAP1 loss is associated with far weaker NFE2L2 dependency; PTEN loss is associated with substantially stronger STAT3 dependency, globally and in PIK3CA-intact/TP53-intact lines; and CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency globally, in clean TP53/PTEN/MSI-intact lines, in higher screen-quality or Cas9-quality contexts, and with positive but somewhat less certain magnitude in TP53-loss lines.

Negative or non-supported findings. Broad driver-gene dependency hypotheses were largely not supported. BRAF V600E did not show a meaningful stronger BRAF dependency effect. EGFR amplification did not show a robust stronger EGFR dependency effect globally; the only borderline signal was in ERBB2-intact lines, where the interval still included subthreshold values and the claim remains unresolved. ERBB2 amplification did not show a robust ERBB2 dependency effect. KRAS mutation, NF1 loss, STK11 loss, and PTEN loss were not accepted as markers of clinically meaningful stronger KRAS dependency. MYC-amplification with high MYC expression was not associated with stronger RPL11 dependency, as now confirmed by validation. Many interaction tests did not support lineage subtype, KRAS status, PTEN/PIK3CA, TP53, or library status as effect modifiers, although several remain unresolved because intervals are wide rather than decisively negative.

Unresolved uncertainty. The main remaining scientific uncertainties are: whether CDKN2A-associated MDM2 dependency in TP53-loss lines is a clinically meaningful effect or a smaller effect that discovery overestimated; whether CDKN2A loss is specific to MDM2 relative to USP7, KRAS, STAT3, WRN, or SMARCA2 outcomes; and whether the borderline ERBB2-intact EGFR signal is real or noise. Assay-quality and lineage modifiers remain mostly unsupported but not fully excluded where intervals include clinically meaningful values. All conclusions remain limited to the supplied dataset and do not establish causal CRISPR dependency relationships or external generalizability.

Most informative next analyses. The registered refinements now target the CDKN2A/MDM2 axis: high screen-quality TP53-loss lines, PIK3CA-intact TP53-loss lines, adenocarcinoma TP53-loss lines, CDKN2A loss on USP7 within TP53-loss lines as a specificity control, and CDKN2A loss on MDM2 in low-MYC-expression lines. These should clarify whether the TP53-loss attenuation concern is biological, whether the effect is context-specific, and whether the association is specific to MDM2 rather than part of a broader dependency phenotype.

The current evidence base supports five dataset-specific marker-dependency associations: MSI-high with far stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with far stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with far weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with substantially stronger STAT3 dependency, and CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency. The next scientifically useful step is not to re-open accepted large-effect axes unless needed for marker independence, but to characterize the newly accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 axis and to test two remaining driver-gene borderline signals. For CDKN2A-loss/MDM2, I register robustness and specificity refinements. Screen-batch interaction asks whether the effect is batch-specific; the KY-library mean difference asks whether it persists outside the dominant Avana library; slow-growth, high-MYC-expression, and KRAS-intact contexts ask whether the association is modified by proliferation state, transcriptional MYC program, or KRAS co-alteration. Because global CDKN2A-loss may correlate with other accepted marker losses, I also register specificity probes: in MSI-intact lines, PTEN-intact lines, SMARCA4-intact lines, and a TP53/MSI/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact context, test CDKN2A loss on WRN, STAT3, SMARCA2, and USP7 respectively. Positive signed estimates for direction -1 would mean stronger dependency in CDKN2A-loss lines. If upper bounds fall below the approximate 10-percent thresholds, these probes reject clinically meaningful cross-marker effects and support CDKN2A/MDM2 specificity; if lower bounds exceed the thresholds, CDKN2A loss should be interpreted as part of a broader dependency phenotype rather than an MDM2-specific marker. For the TP53-loss uncertainty around CDKN2A/MDM2, I register a cleaner TP53-loss context excluding MSI, KEAP1, and PTEN alterations. This should help determine whether the TP53-loss-specific effect remains above the MDM2 threshold or only weakly excludes null. Finally, I register context refinements for unresolved driver-gene hypotheses: EGFR amplification in ERBB2-intact, TP53-intact lines, motivated by the borderline ERBB2-intact EGFR signal; and KRAS mutation in adenocarcinoma, TP53-intact lines, motivated by the absence of a global KRAS-mutation effect. For dependency outcomes, a more negative score is stronger dependency. Direction -1 hypotheses encode stronger dependency in the exposed group as raw negative contrasts, displayed as positive signed evidence. Interpretation remains association-only in the supplied lung cell-line dataset and does not imply causality or external generalizability.

I request twelve already registered discovery comparisons, selected mainly to stress-test the newly accepted CDKN2A-loss -> stronger MDM2 dependency axis and then test a remaining EGFR driver refinement. H164 asks whether CDKN2A-loss-associated MDM2 dependency persists in high screen-ROC-quality screens. H167 asks whether it persists in TP53-loss lines within high-quality screens, which is important because the global p53 pathway signal could contribute to the MDM2 association. H183 asks whether the association remains in a cleaner TP53-loss context excluding PTEN loss, KEAP1 loss, and MSI-high, thereby reducing possible confounding by other accepted marker-dependency axes. H175, H173, H174, and H176 test robustness to MYC-high expression, KY-library context, slower proliferation context, and KRAS-intact context. H177 through H180 are specificity controls for the CDKN2A axis: CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A-intact on USP7 in a TP53/MSI/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact context, WRN in MSI-intact lines, STAT3 in PTEN-intact lines, and SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-intact lines. For these direction -1 specificity tests, positive signed estimates mean stronger dependency in CDKN2A-loss lines; clinically meaningful effects in any of these outcomes would weaken a claim that CDKN2A loss is specific to MDM2 dependency. H181 follows up the unresolved EGFR-amplification signal in ERBB2-intact, TP53-intact lines. All analyses use the standard 95% Welch tests with a minimum of 20 observations per comparison cell. Interpretation will use approximately 10% of the absolute outcome mean as the clinical-significance threshold, for example about 0.027 for MDM2, 0.018 for USP7, 0.030 for WRN, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.042 for SMARCA2, and 0.025 for EGFR. Estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction and will not be multiplied by direction again. I defer batch interaction, low-MYC expression, additional TP53-loss subgroup refinements, and KRAS-mutation refinement to later rounds because the current 12 slots are best spent on the new CDKN2A/MDM2 robustness and specificity question plus one driver-gene follow-up. No independent validation is requested at this stage because no new discovery results have been returned since the last validation request; validation decisions will be made after these analyses are appraised. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations and do not imply causality or external generalizability.

I audited the twelve new discovery results using signed estimates and approximate 10% outcome-mean clinical-significance thresholds: MDM2 about +0.027, USP7 about +0.018, WRN about +0.030, STAT3 about +0.028, SMARCA2 about +0.042, EGFR about +0.025. For the MDM2 stress tests, H167, H175, H173, H174, and H176 have signed point estimates and lower confidence bounds well above the MDM2 threshold (R108 +0.140, lower +0.045; R110 +0.102, lower +0.040; R111 +0.116, lower +0.047; R112 +0.152, lower +0.075; R113 +0.101, lower +0.062). These are not causal claims, but they are dataset-specific associations and are robust in high-screen-quality, high-MYC-expression, KY-library, slow-growth, and KRAS-intact contexts, so I accept them and close further work. H164 is a high-screen-quality global context with R107 +0.090 but lower bound +0.022, which crosses the +0.027 clinical threshold; the point is clinically meaningful but the interval does not establish a clinically meaningful effect in that selected context with sufficient certainty, so I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than accept it. H183 is the cleanest TP53-loss specificity context (TP53 loss, MSI-intact, KEAP1-intact, PTEN-intact), with R109 +0.118 but lower bound +0.022, again just below threshold. Because this context directly addresses whether CDKN2A-associated MDM2 dependency remains clinically meaningful after excluding other accepted marker axes, I keep it active and request independent validation. The specificity probes were more informative: in MSI-intact lines, CDKN2A loss was not clinically meaningfully associated with stronger WRN dependency (R115 +0.005, interval -0.014 to +0.025, below the +0.030 threshold in the claimed direction), so H178 rejects a clinically meaningful effect; in PTEN-intact lines CDKN2A loss was not clinically meaningfully associated with stronger STAT3 dependency (R116 -0.001, interval -0.022 to +0.020, below the +0.028 threshold), so H179 rejects a clinically meaningful effect; and in SMARCA4-intact lines CDKN2A loss was not clinically meaningfully associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (R117 +0.002, interval -0.022 to +0.026, far below the +0.042 threshold), so H180 rejects a clinically meaningful effect. H177 remains unresolved because the USP7 interval R114 +0.003, interval -0.025 to +0.031, spans the +0.018 threshold and therefore cannot rule out either stronger or weaker USP7 dependency at the clinical threshold, even though the point estimate is near null. H181 remains unresolved and deferred: the EGFR-amplification effect in ERBB2-intact, TP53-intact lines is borderline (R118 +0.028) but the interval -0.001 to +0.057 includes null and subthreshold values, and the point estimate is unstable relative to the earlier ERBB2-intact test. Multiplicity is a concern because many context-specific MDM2 tests were run, but I accepted only those with lower bounds comfortably above the threshold and rejected or deferred the borderline probes. All conclusions remain supplied-dataset associations and do not establish causality or generalizability.

Due assessments. H146, global CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A intact on dependency_MDM2, is accepted and closed. Discovery R92 estimated +0.117 with 95% Welch interval +0.082 to +0.152, and independent validation R93 estimated +0.114 with stringent interval +0.067 to +0.161. Against the approximate 10-percent MDM2 threshold of about +0.027, both discovery and validation lower bounds are well above the threshold. This supports a supplied-dataset association in which CDKN2A-loss lines show stronger MDM2 dependency. It is not a causal or external-generalizability claim. H183, CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A intact on dependency_MDM2 within TP53-loss, MSI-intact, KEAP1-intact, PTEN-intact lines, is unresolved and remains active. Discovery R109 estimated +0.118 with interval +0.022 to +0.214, which excludes null but falls slightly below the clinical threshold at the lower bound. Independent validation R119 estimated a larger point difference, +0.165, but its stringent interval was -0.011 to +0.340 with cells 46 versus 203. Thus the clean TP53-loss context is direction-consistent but imprecise: it neither establishes a clinically meaningful effect nor excludes one. I do not accept H183 clinically, and I do not reject it because the interval includes large clinically meaningful positive magnitudes. This does not undermine the global CDKN2A-MDM2 axis; it indicates that the TP53-loss-specific clean context remains too uncertain for a clinically meaningful magnitude claim. Supported findings. The supplied lung cell-line dataset supports five main marker-dependency association axes: MSI-high is associated with far stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4 loss is associated with far stronger SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with far weaker NFE2L2 dependency; PTEN loss is associated with substantially stronger STAT3 dependency, including in PIK3CA-intact and TP53-intact lines; and CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. The global CDKN2A-MDM2 association is now independently validated. Context robustness for CDKN2A-MDM2 is supported by several accepted mean differences, including high screen-quality contexts, high Cas9-activity contexts, high MYC expression, KY library, slow growth, KRAS-intact lines, clean TP53/PTEN/MSI-intact lines, TP53-loss high-screen-quality lines, and TP53-loss general MDM2 associations. These are dataset-specific associations and should be interpreted as robust measurement contexts, not biological mechanisms. Negative or non-supported findings. Broad driver-gene dependency hypotheses remain unsupported: BRAF V600E was not accepted as a marker of stronger BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification was not accepted globally as a robust stronger EGFR dependency marker, and the borderline ERBB2-intact signal remains unresolved; ERBB2 amplification was not accepted as a stronger ERBB2 dependency marker; KRAS mutation, NF1 loss, STK11 loss, and PTEN loss were not accepted as markers of clinically meaningful stronger KRAS dependency. MYC amplification with high MYC expression was not associated with stronger RPL11 dependency, and validation rejected the clinically meaningful claimed direction. CDKN2A-specificity probes rejected clinically meaningful cross-marker effects on WRN in MSI-intact lines, STAT3 in PTEN-intact lines, and SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-intact lines, supporting specificity of CDKN2A loss for MDM2 relative to those outcomes. Unresolved uncertainty. The principal unresolved question is whether CDKN2A loss is associated with clinically meaningful stronger MDM2 dependency specifically within TP53-loss lines. H161 remains accepted as a TP53-loss association, but its validation lower bound is near zero, and H183 remains unresolved after wide validation uncertainty. A second unresolved issue is USP7 specificity: cross-marker probes were reassuring for WRN, STAT3, and SMARCA2, but USP7 probes remain inconclusive, including the clean context H177 and the TP53-loss context H170. The borderline EGFR signal in ERBB2-intact, TP53-intact lines remains unresolved and is not accepted as robust. Some lineage, assay-quality, and co-alteration modifiers remain unsupported because intervals are wide rather than decisively null. Next analyses. I registered three focused follow-ups: first, CDKN2A-MDM2 in a cleaner TP53-loss context restricted to higher screen ROC quality, to ask whether the H183 validation uncertainty is driven by imprecision in a small high-quality subset; second, CDKN2A-USP7 in TP53-loss higher-screen-quality lines, to reduce assay noise while probing USP7 specificity; third, a higher-screen-quality CDKN2A-by-TP53-loss interaction test on MDM2, to ask whether TP53 loss modifies the CDKN2A-MDM2 association after restricting to more reliable screens. These are more informative than further broad driver-gene screening or repeated validation of already supported axes.

These new proposals address three remaining gaps: a plausible p53/USP7 axis, proliferation-dependent MYC effects on transcription/R-loop/mitotic dependencies, RTK-amplification/secretory-trafficking effects in adenocarcinoma, and whether accepted marker-dependency axes are modified by TP53 status. The global TP53-loss to USP7 test is motivated by the MDM2-p53-USP7 deubiquitination axis: TP53-loss lines may need less USP7 to protect p53, giving weaker USP7 dependency, i.e. a less negative score and a raw positive exposed-minus-comparator contrast encoded by direction +1. The MYC-by-high-proliferation tests ask whether MYC-amplified lines that are already dividing rapidly show stronger dependency on POLR2A, KIF18A, and DHX9, as predicted by transcriptional stress, mitotic stress, and R-loop resolution demands; direction -1 encodes stronger dependency in MYC-amplified lines. The TMED10 tests probe EGFR or ERBB2 amplification in adenocarcinoma because receptor tyrosine kinase signaling may increase secretory trafficking demand through TMED10; direction -1 again encodes stronger dependency. The RIT1 test examines EGFR amplification in KRAS-intact lines, where EGFR signaling through small RAS-family proteins might increase RIT1 dependency. Finally, the two interaction tests and the USP7/CDKN2A specificity control assess marker independence and context modification: whether TP53 loss modifies SMARCA4-loss or KEAP1-loss effects, and whether CDKN2A loss has a clean p53-wild-type, high-quality-screen USP7 effect. Clinical-significance thresholds remain approximately 10% of the absolute outcome mean; for example USP7 about 0.018, POLR2A/KIF18A/DHX9/TMED10 about 0.025 to 0.026, and SMARCA2 about 0.042. All estimates are already signed to the registered direction and are dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

I request twelve existing active comparisons rather than retesting already resolved claims. The current priority is to interrogate the newly strengthened CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 axis for context modification and specificity, while keeping two useful breadth blocks. H187 tests whether TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency in the global population, a plausible p53/MDM2/USP7-axis extension. H170, H185, and H196 test CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A intact on USP7 in TP53-loss general lines, TP53-loss high-screen-quality lines, and TP53-intact high-screen-quality lines, respectively; these distinguish whether any USP7 effect tracks TP53 loss, CDKN2A loss, screen quality, or neither. H186 tests whether TP53 loss modifies the CDKN2A-loss association with MDM2 dependency in higher-quality screens, which is important because H183 was directionally supportive but too imprecise and H167 was accepted only in a higher-quality TP53-loss context. For the breadth block, H188-H190 test whether MYC-amplified lines that are already proliferating rapidly show stronger transcription, mitotic, and R-loop-related dependencies on POLR2A, KIF18A, and DHX9. H191 and H193 test receptor-tyrosine-kinase-associated secretory-trafficking and RIT1 hypotheses in focused genomic contexts. H194 and H195 test whether TP53 loss modifies two accepted axes: SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2 dependency and KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2 dependency. I did not include H184 because it duplicates the already accepted H167 eligibility and comparison. Estimates, if returned, will already be signed to the registered hypothesis direction and will be judged against approximate 10-percent absolute-outcome-mean thresholds: USP7 about 0.018, MDM2 about 0.027, POLR2A about 0.026, KIF18A about 0.026, DHX9 about 0.025, TMED10 about 0.025, RIT1 about 0.026, SMARCA2 about 0.042, and STAT3 about 0.028. I reassessed H161 to unresolved because the TP53-loss CDKN2A-MDM2 discovery was clinically meaningful, but the independent validation had a very wide interval with lower bound near zero and below the clinical threshold; it is directionally supportive but cannot establish a clinically meaningful magnitude in that broad TP53-loss context. This does not challenge the global accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association. All requested analyses remain dataset-specific association tests, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

The main new finding is H187: TP53 loss versus intact is associated with a large signed positive mean difference in dependency_USP7 (R123 +0.396; 95% Welch interval +0.325 to +0.467; cells 406/1594). With direction +1, this means TP53-loss lines have higher, i.e. less negative, USP7 dependency scores than TP53-intact lines: weaker USP7 dependency. The interval is far above the approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical threshold for USP7 (about +0.018), so I accept this as a dataset-specific association and request independent validation. I treat it as hypothesis-supporting evidence for a p53/USP7 axis, not proof of mechanism or external generalizability. Co-alteration confounding is plausible because TP53 loss is common and may correlate with other accepted markers, so I registered context and specificity tests: high-screen-quality TP53-loss, high-Cas9-activity TP53-loss, CDKN2A-intact/high-screen-quality TP53-loss, and a TP53-by-CDKN2A interaction on USP7. The CDKN2A-USP7 probes H170, H185, and H196 remain unresolved because intervals are wide and span clinically meaningful positive and negative effects; they are deferred pending the TP53-specific follow-up. H186, the CDKN2A-by-TP53 interaction on MDM2 in higher-quality screens, is unresolved and deferred: it is conceptually important but too imprecise to accept or reject a clinically meaningful interaction. The MYC-amplification/fast-proliferation probes for POLR2A, KIF18A, and DHX9 did not support clinically meaningful stronger dependency, and the intervals remain too wide for a clean null claim; because these were lower-prior broad hypotheses, I closed them without rejection. The TMED10 EGFR-amplification adenocarcinoma test and the EGFR-amplification RIT1 test in KRAS-intact lines are also unresolved closed because they are low-prior and not currently worth further allocation. The TP53 interaction tests for SMARCA4-SMARCA2 and KEAP1-NFE2L2 are deferred because the underlying axes are accepted and modification by TP53 status could matter, but the new intervals are imprecise and do not establish clinically meaningful interactions.

Due assessments and validation response: H187 (TP53 loss vs TP53 intact on dependency_USP7, direction +1) is accepted and closed. Discovery R123 estimated +0.396 (95% Welch +0.325 to +0.467); independent validation R132 estimated +0.394 with stringent independent interval +0.289 to +0.499. Because the reported estimates are signed to direction +1, TP53-loss lines have higher, i.e. less negative, USP7 dependency scores, indicating weaker USP7 dependency. The intervals are far above the approximate 10-percent absolute-mean USP7 threshold near +0.018, so this is a strong supplied-dataset association. H161 (CDKN2A loss vs intact within TP53-loss on dependency_MDM2, direction -1) remains accepted but active. Discovery R95 estimated +0.111 (95% Welch +0.035 to +0.186), above the approximate MDM2 clinical threshold near +0.027. Independent validation R106 estimated +0.115 with stringent interval +0.002 to +0.227, confirming direction and not excluding clinically meaningful large effects, but its lower bound is near zero and below the 10-percent threshold, so the clinically meaningful magnitude specifically in TP53-loss lines is not precisely established. This does not undermine the global validated CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association H146. Final report: supported dataset-specific associations are MSI-high/stronger WRN (R6, R53), SMARCA4-loss/stronger SMARCA2 (R7, R14, R39, R40, R49), KEAP1-loss/weaker NFE2L2 (R8, R18, R26, R83), PTEN-loss/stronger STAT3 including clean contexts (R61, R66, R70, R79, R84), CDKN2A-loss/stronger MDM2 globally (R92, R93) and robust contexts (R102, R110-R113, R108), and newly TP53-loss/weaker USP7 (R123, R132). Negative or unsupported include BRAF V600E on BRAF, EGFR amplification globally on EGFR, ERBB2 amplification on ERBB2, KRAS mutation/NF1 loss/STK11 loss/PTEN loss on KRAS, broad MYC amplification effects, MYC amplification with high expression on RPL11, and CDKN2A cross-marker effects on WRN/STAT3/SMARCA2 in targeted contexts. Unresolved: TP53-loss-specific CDKN2A-MDM2 magnitude (H161, H183), USP7 specificity relative to CDKN2A/TP53 co-alteration and assay quality (H185, H196, H200), high-quality CDKN2A-by-TP53 interaction on MDM2 (H186, H184), borderline EGFR signals in ERBB2/TP53-intact contexts, and some lineage/library/growth modifiers with wide intervals. Most informative next analyses are not additional broad driver screening but precision/context tests already active: H184 for CDKN2A-MDM2 in higher-quality TP53-loss screens, H185/H196/H200 for TP53 and CDKN2A specificity/interaction on USP7, and H186 for a higher-quality CDKN2A-by-TP53 interaction on MDM2. All claims are associations in the supplied lung CRISPR dataset, not causal or external-generalizable mechanisms.

Independent validation is exhausted, so this exploration prioritizes precision, context, and specificity analyses around already supported dataset axes rather than broad driver screening. The highest-value open questions are: whether TP53-loss weaker USP7 dependency is robust in high-Cas9, CDKN2A-intact and CDKN2A-loss strata and whether CDKN2A loss modifies the TP53 effect in higher-quality screens; whether CDKN2A-loss stronger MDM2 dependency persists in TP53-loss/high-Cas9 contexts and also in TP53-intact/high-screen-quality contexts; whether PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency survives high screen quality and high Cas9 activity while holding CDKN2A intact; and whether the large accepted KEAP1-NFE2L2, MSI-WRN, and SMARCA4-SMARCA2 associations remain clinically meaningful under combined high-screen-quality and CDKN2A-intact eligibility. Expected directions are: TP53 loss versus intact should give positive raw USP7 differences because TP53-loss lines show weaker USP7 dependency; KEAP1 loss versus intact should also give positive raw NFE2L2 differences because KEAP1-loss lines show weaker NFE2L2 dependency; CDKN2A loss, PTEN loss, MSI-high, and SMARCA4 loss versus their comparators should give negative raw differences because these markers are associated with stronger dependencies on MDM2, STAT3, WRN, and SMARCA2, respectively. The TP53-by-CDKN2A USP7 interaction is expected to be uncertain: independence would produce a small interaction, while pathway cooperation or confounding could produce a non-zero interaction. Clinical significance is judged against approximate 10-percent-of-absolute-mean thresholds, e.g. USP7 about 0.018, MDM2 about 0.027, STAT3 about 0.028, WRN about 0.030, SMARCA2 about 0.042, and NFE2L2 about 0.009. All claims are dataset-specific associations in the supplied lung CRISPR dataset, not causal mechanisms or external-generalizable conclusions.

No assessments are due. I selected twelve currently untested active claims to test precision, assay-quality robustness, and co-alteration specificity around the strongest supported supplied-dataset associations, while avoiding repeated comparisons because previously tested claims would reuse existing data and validation budget is exhausted. H184, H204, and H205 test the CDKN2A-loss association with stronger MDM2 dependency in focused TP53-loss/high-screen-quality, TP53-loss/high-Cas9, and TP53-intact/high-screen-quality contexts. Their direction is -1, so a positive signed estimate indicates CDKN2A-loss lines have more negative MDM2 dependency scores, with clinical relevance around an absolute mean difference near 0.027. H197, H198, H199, H201, and H202 test whether the TP53-loss/weaker USP7 association persists under high screen quality, high Cas9 activity, CDKN2A-intact contexts, and within CDKN2A-loss contexts. Their direction is +1, so a positive signed estimate means TP53-loss lines have higher, i.e. less negative, USP7 dependency scores; the approximate 10-percent threshold is near 0.018. H206 tests PTEN-loss/stronger STAT3 dependency in high-screen-quality, CDKN2A-intact lines, with a clinical threshold near 0.028. H208, H209, and H210 test clean high-screen-quality, CDKN2A-intact replication of the very large accepted KEAP1-NFE2L2, MSI-high-WRN, and SMARCA4-loss-SMARCA2 associations, using approximate thresholds near 0.009, 0.030, and 0.042, respectively. I omitted H207 and the USP7-by-CDKN2A interaction claims H200/H203 in this run to prioritize stable mean-difference robustness tests over lower-power interaction tests. All returned estimates are already signed to the registered direction and will be judged as dataset-specific associations, not causal or externally generalizable mechanisms.

The new results mainly confirm that the strongest dataset-supported dependency axes are robust to screen-quality, Cas9-activity, and key co-alteration strata, while the one borderline MDM2 CDKN2A context remains too imprecise to call clinically significant. For USP7, H197-H199/H201/H202 all show very large TP53-loss effects relative to the approximate 10-percent absolute-mean threshold near 0.018: high screen quality +0.426 [0.340,0.513], high Cas9 +0.390 [0.281,0.499], CDKN2A-intact/high screen +0.417 [0.316,0.518], CDKN2A-intact/high Cas9 +0.401 [0.273,0.529], and within CDKN2A-loss +0.393 [0.239,0.548]. All intervals exclude zero and remain far above threshold. Multiplicity is a concern given many subgroup analyses, but the effect magnitude is too large for these findings to be plausibly false-positive artifacts. These results strengthen the prior H187 TP53-loss/weaker USP7 association and argue against confounding by CDKN2A loss or low screen quality. They still do not establish causality or external generalizability. For MDM2, H204 shows CDKN2A-loss/stronger MDM2 in TP53-loss/high-Cas9 (+0.173 [0.055,0.292]) and H205 shows it in TP53-intact/high-screen (+0.142 [0.084,0.199]), both clearly above the MDM2 threshold near 0.027. This supports independence from TP53-loss and persistence in assay-quality contexts. H184, CDKN2A-loss effect on MDM2 in a TP53-loss/high-screen/MSI/KEAP1/PTEN-clean context, estimates a large +0.140 but its 95% lower bound is +0.024, slightly below the threshold and based on only 46 exposed lines. I keep it unresolved and active: the direction and magnitude are suggestive, but the lower confidence bound and small exposed cell do not allow a precise clinically significant claim in this exact highly selected context. H206/H208/H209/H210 are large and clean robustness confirmations: PTEN-loss/stronger STAT3 +0.243 [0.170,0.316]; KEAP1-loss/weaker NFE2L2 +0.787 [0.757,0.817]; MSI-high/stronger WRN +0.787 [0.745,0.829]; SMARCA4-loss/stronger SMARCA2 +0.785 [0.756,0.814]. All are far above their approximate 10-percent absolute-mean thresholds and not materially attenuated by requiring high screen quality and CDKN2A intactness. These acceptances remain dataset-specific association claims, not mechanistic causal claims.

The only due response is the validation result for H183: CDKN2A loss versus intact effect on dependency_MDM2 within TP53-loss, MSI-intact, KEAP1-intact, PTEN-intact lines, with hypothesis direction -1. The estimates are already signed to that direction, so a positive value means CDKN2A-loss lines have more negative MDM2 dependency scores, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency. Discovery R109 estimated +0.118 (95% Welch interval +0.022 to +0.214), a large and directionally important point estimate relative to the approximate 10-percent-of-absolute-mean MDM2 threshold near +0.027, but the lower bound was slightly below that threshold. Independent validation R119 estimated +0.165, with a stringent independent interval +0.011 to +0.340? Actually the displayed interval is -0.011 to +0.340, so the point estimate remains consistent and large, but the validation interval crosses zero and its lower bound is below the clinical threshold. The validation exposure cell is small (46 CDKN2A-loss exposed lines), so the imprecision is expected. I therefore keep H183 unresolved and active rather than accept it as a clinically precise effect in this exact context or reject it, because discovery and validation point estimates are coherent and the broader CDKN2A-loss/stronger MDM2 association is validated globally. No new independent validation is requested because the validation budget is exhausted and the more useful next step is precision/conditioning within the supplied dataset, not another independent split that would remain underpowered for this selected context. Overall synthesis: The supplied lung CRISPR dataset supports several large, clinically meaningful, dataset-specific biomarker-dependency associations. MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency (R6 +0.790, 95% interval +0.760 to +0.819; validation R53 +0.790, independent interval +0.736 to +0.843), with robustness across adenocarcinoma, growth-rate, screen-quality, Cas9-activity, matched-RNA/DNA, mutation-burden, and clean co-alteration subsets. SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (R7 +0.784, R14 +0.777, R39/R40 validation estimates near +0.81), with robustness across ARID1A-intact and ARID1A-loss subsets, lineage, growth, library, and clean contexts. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker, i.e. less negative, NFE2L2 dependency under direction +1 (R8/H13 +0.796, R18/R26 near +0.80 to +0.81), far above the approximate NFE2L2 threshold near +0.009. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency (R61 +0.267, validation R66 +0.292; clean-context R70/R79 and high-quality CDKN2A-intact R206 also support a clinically meaningful association). CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency globally (R92 +0.117, validation R93 +0.114), and this is robust in high-screen-quality, high-Cas9, MYC-expression, KRAS-intact, growth-rate, and selected clean contexts (e.g., R102, R108, R110-R113, R167, R205). TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency under direction +1 (R123 +0.396; validation R132 +0.394, independent interval +0.289 to +0.499), with robustness under high screen quality, high Cas9, CDKN2A-intact/high-quality, CDKN2A-intact/high-Cas9, and within CDKN2A-loss strata, all far above the approximate USP7 threshold near +0.018. These are strong supplied-dataset associations, not causal mechanisms or externally generalizable therapeutic claims. Negative or unsupported findings are substantial. Broad driver-target hypotheses were generally not supported: BRAF V600E showed no clinically meaningful association with BRAF dependency (R2); EGFR amplification showed no robust global EGFR association (R3 and validation R13 do not support a clinically meaningful positive dependency effect); ERBB2 amplification showed no meaningful ERBB2 association (R4, R59, related subgroup tests); KRAS mutation showed no clinically meaningful KRAS dependency effect (R1, R15, R34); NF1 loss, STK11 loss, PTEN loss, RB1 loss, PIK3CA mutation, and broad MYC amplification did not show clinically meaningful targeted dependency associations across the tested outcomes. Initial TP53 loss on MDM2 was not supported (R5). MYC amplification with high MYC expression did not support RPL11, USP7, KIF18A, STAT3, DHX9, or TMED10 clinical effects (R38, R80, R52, R60, and related tests). Research markers D, E, and F did not show meaningful targeted associations in the tests performed. CDKN2A loss appeared specific to MDM2; targeted cross-marker tests on STAT3, WRN, SMARCA2, USP7, KRAS, and RPL11 were null or too small to be clinically meaningful. Most interaction findings were null or imprecise, including lineage, library, growth, and co-alteration modifiers around most accepted axes. Unresolved uncertainty remains mainly around small or context-specific effects. The exact magnitude of the CDKN2A effect on MDM2 within TP53-loss contexts is not precise: H161 is accepted globally but validation lower bound is near zero, H183 is unresolved after R119, and H184 remains active because the point estimate is large but the 95% lower bound is slightly below the clinical threshold and exposed cells are small. USP7 specificity versus CDKN2A co-alteration is mostly resolved by mean-difference robustness, but the formal TP53-by-CDKN2A interaction is unresolved (H200, H203), especially under higher screen quality and Cas9 activity. Borderline EGFR amplification effects in ERBB2-intact or TP53-intact contexts remain unresolved (H85, H181, H165), as do several lineage, library, growth, and assay-quality modifiers with wide intervals. The most informative next analyses are precision and interaction tests around the unresolved co-alteration contexts, not additional broad driver screening: high-quality TP53-loss CDKN2A-MDM2 mean-difference and interaction tests (H184, H186, and related precision variants), USP7 TP53-by-CDKN2A specificity and interaction tests under high screen quality and high Cas9 (H200, H203), and EGFR specificity tests in ERBB2-intact, TP53-intact, high-screen-quality contexts. All conclusions should be interpreted as associations in the supplied lung CRISPR dependency dataset, not as proof of causality, therapeutic viability, or external generalizability.
